title: Culture Matters in Toxic Language Detection in Persian
benchmark_measurement: The study evaluated models on their ability to detect toxic language in Persian, with a specific focus on how cultural context impacts performance. A key measurement related to faith/religion was the detection of hate speech targeting religious groups, particularly in cross-lingual transfer learning experiments from Arabic to Persian.
findings: Transfer learning from a language with shared cultural context (Arabic) significantly improves the detection of hate speech in Persian, especially for content related to religious and political topics. This suggests that shared cultural understanding, including religious context, is more beneficial for performance than simply using a high-resource language like English.
